claim: The requirement asks for all generated code to carry `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`, but every template wraps the attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. Projects targeting netstandard2.0 or any .NET Framework TFM therefore get undecorated formatters and resolvers. The attribute is available on both: netstandard2.0 exposes `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute`, and .NET Framework 4.0+ has it in mscorlib with AttributeUsage that includes Class. So the derived criterion ('the attribute must exist there or be conditionally emitted') does not justify excluding these targets. netstandard2.0 is the most common library target, so a large share of users get no benefit.

claim: The generated resolver is a `partial class` that completes a user-written declaration (`[GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class MyResolver { }`). The generated half now always carries `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, and that attribute has AllowMultiple=false. A user who already put `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on their own partial declaration therefore gets CS0579 'Duplicate ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute' and the project no longer compiles. Users following the issue's workaround advice are exactly the ones likely to have done this, so this is a breaking change. The same applies to the CompositeResolverTemplate partial class.
